subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What request-scoped no-side-effects contract should OpenClaw expose for global agent dry-run across CLI, Gateway/embedded runs, built-in/plugin/client tools, direct tool invoke, hosted runtime bridges, and hook behavior?
rationale: This would become a user-trusted security boundary, and source inspection shows multiple execution paths that a narrow process-global adapter flag would not safely cover.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, and hook behavior.

options.title: Fold into broader safe workflow modes
options.body: Keep this issue open but defer implementation until broader Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent mode defines the shared preview vocabulary and guarantees.

options.title: Reject global dry-run
options.body: Leave scoped command-level dry-runs only if maintainers decide a global preview boundary is too easy to misunderstand as a full sandbox guarantee.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, and hook behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans the agent CLI, Gateway tool invoke, and core security/product contract surfaces where this history is strongest.
